status: Proposal only; migrate only after checkpoint and read-lifecycle owner coordination.
first_slice: Persistent byte-exact mutation journal plus scoped single-file write/multiEdit/copy/move/delete and host undo; recursive structural operations follow on the same journal, not a separate irreversible shortcut.

components.name: Immutable mutation context
fields: tool name and normalized input hash
components.reason: Never infer provenance from mutable current ToolExecutor state or reused provider IDs. Capture workspace identity before asynchronous work.

components.name: ScopedMutationPlan / native filesystem backend
components.responsibility: Resolve both operands through one host-owned mount registry. Check source and destination rights independently; plan descendant paths/types through ScopedDirectory with bounded no-follow traversal. Hold validated parents and validate opened file identity. Stage bytes and capture missing/file/directory kinds explicitly.
components.windows_probe_required: Use SetFileInformationByHandle for rename/delete on validated handles; FILE_RENAME_INFO documents a destination directory handle for relative names. Validate actual MinGW/NTFS behavior with fixture probes before selecting final commit primitive. New-file creation and directory creation need contained parent authority throughout; do not reuse resolve-close-QSaveFile path checks as a security guarantee.

components.name: FileMutationJournal
components.storage: Profile-owned SQLite operations/mutations tables and content-addressed exact byte blobs outside ws/apps/att. One serialized native worker owns its DB connection. Record schema/provenance and directory topology. Missing/empty/binary are separate states. Share no agent-readable blob paths.
components.policy: Persist complete before states and operation manifest before first destructive step. Never evict blobs reachable by undo history. Explicit disk/batch limits reject before mutation; do not copy upstream post-mutation history truncation.

components.name: Mutation coordinator
rules: Single-file replacement is atomic where the tested native primitive permits; multi-file changes are recoverable, not claimed as a filesystem-wide atomic transaction
Preflight overlap, permissions, quota, types and complete snapshots before changes. Snapshot conflicting destination contents as well as move source contents
For cross-volume move, finish destination verification before source removal; all steps retain recovery records
On error/cancel before commit, roll back recorded changes only when current identity/content matches the expected staged state; report conflicts instead of overwriting unrelated concurrent edits
After commit, emit one owned result and observers only after journal durability; cancellation then cannot honestly claim no filesystem effect
At startup detect incomplete mutations and recover against recorded identities/hashes; never apply recorded paths to a remapped current ws1 root

components.name: Undo and diff projection
components.responsibility: Select operations by agent plus dispatch/tool-call provenance; replay to the state before earliest selected call, including both move sides, overwritten targets and empty directories. Preserve original history and append undo/restore records. Keep native API/error for unavailable original mount rather than silently resolving a new workspace root.
components.compatibility: Maintain upstream file summaries and internal-mount visibility filters separately from recovery retention. Ignored files still need recovery storage for a destructive operation advertised as undoable. Conflict handling and topology restoration are deliberate native improvements, disclosed in the parity ledger.

components.name: Tool transport/adapters
components.responsibility: Expose upstream names and schemas: copy with required move boolean, delete, write, multiEdit. Return structured message/result/_diff data; preserve legacy fileChanged only as an observer bridge. Keep raw sandbox fs.writeFile/writeBytes byte-exact and free of code-fence stripping. Add native fs.copy/rename/unlink adapters only when their distinct Node contracts and journal attribution are implemented.

integration_order: Finish/read-lifecycle migration and rebase ToolExecutor before editing the shared read dispatch path
Add independent native journal/recovery tests without changing model tool surface
Route write/multiEdit through journal; add exact source message/zero-match/fence fixtures and host undo
Add single-file copy/move/delete with structured results and original mount identity
Add recursive merge/move/delete with all-file records and topology/large binary streaming
Wire native history UI, message reversion, archive finalization and provenance-based edit summary; retain any unimplemented redo/contributor details as gaps
read_lifecycle_boundary: Read snapshots are immutable observations keyed to successful calls; mutation snapshots are durable recovery states. Reuse pure hashing/byte capture where sound, not lease/eviction policy. Do not attach raw sandbox reads or mutation before bytes to provider messages. A mutation invalidates live/editor caches only after commit; previous read captures remain immutable.
open_contract_edges: Empty old_string acceptance versus pinned inconsistent JS behavior
Copy to same object, directory into its own subtree, ancestor/descendant overlaps, case-only rename, hardlinks and symlink/reparse nodes
Mount-root delete/move, permissions metadata and empty-directory topology
Explicit recovery byte/disk budgets and handling oversized binaries without silent truncation
Source parent creation/overwrites versus native no-follow authority constraints
Concurrent external edits and undo conflicts; no undocumented overwrite of user work
